question.problem: Consider the plane curve $2{e}^{xy}=x+y+1.$ Find a tangent vector to that curve at the point $(0,1).$
question.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{e}^{xy} & =x+y+1 \\ 2{e}^{xy}-x-y-1 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y)=2{e}^{xy}-x-y-1$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=0.$ 

A tangent vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(0,1)$ can be computed as follows:

$$
t(0,1)={f}_{y}(0,1)\,i-{f}_{x}(0,1)\,j
$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(0,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(2{e}^{xy}-x-y-1)\,i-\frac{∂}{∂x}(2{e}^{xy}-x-y-1)\,j \\  & =(2x{e}^{xy}-1)\,i-(2y{e}^{xy}-1)\,j \\ t(0,1) & =(2(0){e}^{(0)(1)}-1)\,i-(2(1){e}^{(0)(1)}-1)\,j \\  & =-i-j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our tangent vector is $-i-j.$
